Subject: Post-call: FinTechCo security & encryption requirements

Hi Julie / Aaron —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned:

Call recap (short):
- Primary use: FinTechCo will send LLM inference requests containing limited PII (hashed account IDs, partial SSN for matching flows) and transaction metadata. No large PHI datasets.
- Key security concerns: PII handling, data residency (US-only), retention & audit log retention, and encryption requirements (in-transit, at-rest, customer-managed keys).

Clarifying questions we need answered to scope the proposal:
1) PII categories: can you confirm exact fields you consider PII for this integration (e.g., full name, email, phone, SSN last4 vs full)?
2) Retention: desired retention for inference logs and audit trails (examples: 90 days, 7 years)?
3) Logging scope: do we need full request/response logging stored or only metadata/audit logs? Any redaction policy required?
4) KMS / HSM expectations: do you require Bring-Your-Own-Key (CMEK) with an HSM-backed root key (e.g., CloudHSM), or is cloud KMS (AWS KMS with customer-managed keys) sufficient?

What we can do / next steps:
- We support TLS 1.2+ (recommended 1.3) for in-transit encryption.
- At-rest: AES-256 by default. We offer Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) integration with major cloud KMS providers.
- For stronger HSM-backed root key guarantees we recommend Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) which supports CloudHSM or customer HSM integrations. Hosted can support envelope encryption with your KMS (standard CMEK) — tradeoffs noted below.

Please send the answers to questions 1–4 and any copy of your security questionnaire; I’ve attached our short security one-pager to help. Once we have that, I’ll loop Neha (SE) to put together a concise options doc and propose a follow-up call with your security engineer and CISO.

Best,

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers and notes from our security team:

1) PII scope: We consider full name, email, phone, account_id (internal), and SSN last4 as PII for this integration. We will NOT send full SSN.
2) Retention: Audit logs and request metadata need to be retained for 7 years for compliance reasons. Full request/response payloads should only be kept for 90 days unless explicitly approved.
3) Logging: We need metadata/audit logs (request ID, timestamp, calling service, model used) retained long-term. Full request/response bodies should be redacted after 90 days; for some narrow flows we may request longer retention but that will be on a case-by-case basis.
4) KMS/HSM: Our preference is CMEK backed by an HSM (CloudHSM) or an HSM appliance if you support Private deployments. If hosted CMEK (AWS KMS with customer key) can provide proof that Redwood cannot access plaintext keys and supports envelope encryption, that may be acceptable—our security team needs the specifics.

Attached is our standard security questionnaire and an excerpt of the compliance page. Aaron (cc) will join the next call to discuss the technical details and Dave (CISO) will likely join the decision call.

Julie — really helpful, thank you. Below is a concise mapping of how Redwood can meet each item and the recommended deployment/configuration. Neha, feel free to correct or expand.

PII handling & retention:
- We can support per-route retention policies: metadata/audit logs retained for 7 years; full request/response payloads retained 90 days by default with options for extended retention on a per-flow basis (requires contract/controls).
- Redaction: we can support on-ingest redaction (client-side SDK or server-side rules) to strip specified fields before persisting.

Logging controls:
- Long-term audit logs: immutable audit trails (write-once) stored in encrypted object store, access controlled via RBAC and logged.
- Access: role-based access and cross-team logging only with approvals.

Data residency:
- We can pin workloads to US regions only for hosted. For stricter residency we offer Private deployments (VPC/on-prem).

Encryption & KMS options (summary):
- In-transit: TLS 1.2/1.3 enforced for all API traffic.
- At-rest: AES-256 volume encryption by default.
- Hosted + CMEK: Envelope encryption where data keys are encrypted with your KMS key (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). Redwood does not retain plaintext root keys; we store encrypted DEKs and rotate per policy. This meets many customers’ CMEK requirements.
- Private + HSM: For CloudHSM or customer HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2/3 HSM), we recommend Private deployment—this gives you full control of the key material and guarantees around HSM root-of-trust.

Tradeoffs / notes:
- Hosted CMEK provides strong key separation but cannot provide a physical HSM guarantee in our managed service unless the KMS provider exposes that guarantee (e.g., AWS KMS with CloudHSM-backed keys).
- If FinTechCo requires absolute assurance that Redwood never has the ability to decrypt data without your HSM present, Private deployment with HSM is the recommended path.

Next steps:
1) Neha to draft a short technical options doc (will attach redwood-kms-options.pdf).
2) Schedule a 30-min technical sync with Aaron and Dave to walk through CMEK architecture and confirm retention workflows. Proposed times: Tue 12 Oct 2026 10:00 PT (please confirm).
3) If FinTechCo signs off on hosted CMEK, we’ll prepare contract language for CMEK and retention SLAs; if Private/HSM required, we’ll put together deployment sizing and timeline.

Attachments: [attachment: redwood-kms-options.pdf]

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Internal: KMS/HSM technical notes for FinTechCo (do not forward)

Internal note — summary of implementation details to feed into the options doc and upcoming call:

- Hosted CMEK flow (supported):
  * Customer has KMS (AWS KMS). Redwood requests DEK from KMS using a granted IAM role; DEK is used to encrypt data locally (or within our enclave) and then DEK is re-encrypted with the customer KMS key before storage (envelope encryption).
  * Redwood never stores plaintext KMS root keys. Access to request a DEK requires customer-granted permissions; we support key policy scoping and separate service accounts per customer.
  * Audit trails for all KMS decrypt/encrypt operations can be surfaced via CloudTrail logs (customer-owned) and Redwood logs for our operational actions (metadata only).

- HSM / Private deployment:
  * For CloudHSM-backed keys, recommend Private deployment in customer VPC with dedicated HSM cluster or BYOH (bring-your-own-HSM) connector. This provides cryptographic boundary the security team typically requires.

- Retention enforcement:
  * We can implement automated retention jobs to delete/redact payloads after X days; audit logs export to long-term storage for 7 years. Need legal sign-off on deletion SLA language.

Action items for legal/contract team: confirm CMEK/Cryptography clause language (no plaintext key access by Redwood, key escrow rules, audit rights).
